title: Get Started with GPSA
text: GPSA (Gene-set Perturbation Signature Analysis) provides fast similarity search large-scale perturbation signature databases using cMAP/GSEA-style rankZ semantics. Given query gene set, GPSA finds perturbations (e.g., gene knockouts, drug treatments) produce similar opposite transcriptomic effects. enables: Drug repurposing (find compounds reverse disease signature) Mechanism discovery (identify genes whose perturbation mimics phenotype) Cross-study comparison (compare results public databases)

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: Install GPSA GitHub:
code: # Install remotes if needed if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages("remotes") }  # Install GPSA from GitHub remotes::install_github("Shipeng-Guo/GPSA")

title: Get Started with GPSA
code: # For GSEA visualization (recommended) if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {   install.packages("BiocManager") } BiocManager::install("fgsea")  # For MSigDB gene sets (used in examples) install.packages("msigdbr")  # For advanced plotting install.packages("ggplot2")

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: GPSA requires pre-built HDF5 database containing perturbation signatures. Download database file set path:
code: library(GPSA)  # Set path once (persists for session) options(GPSA.h5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")  # Alternative: environment variable # Sys.setenv(GPSA_H5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: GPSA offers two loading modes:
code: # Memory mode (recommended): ~0.15s per query, ~1GB RAM db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)  # Disk mode: ~7s per query, minimal RAM # db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = FALSE)

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: Let’s find perturbations suppress estrogen signaling. ’ll use Hallmark Estrogen Response Early gene set MSigDB.
code: library(msigdbr)  # Get Hallmark gene sets for human hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H")  # Helper function to extract genes get_hallmark_genes <- function(gs_name) {   unique(hallmark$gene_symbol[hallmark$gs_name == gs_name]) }  # Get estrogen response genes er_genes <- get_hallmark_genes("HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY") message(sprintf("Estrogen Response Early: %d genes", length(er_genes)))

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: find perturbations suppress estrogen signaling, use sign = -1:
code: # Define query: negative sign means we want perturbations where these genes go DOWN query_er_down <- list(   ER_SUPPRESSED = list(     genes = er_genes,     sign = -1,      # Looking for suppression     weight = 1   ) )  # Run search out_er <- gpsa_search(db, query_er_down, return_components = TRUE)  # View top hits (perturbations that suppress estrogen response) message("=== Top 10 Estrogen Suppressors ===") print(head(out_er$res[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName",                            "Score", "tau", "FDR_rank")], 10))

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: negative enrichment score confirms estrogen response genes indeed -regulated perturbation.
code: # Get the logFC profile of the top hit top_hit <- out_er$res$signature_id[1] gl_top <- gpsa_get_signature(db, top_hit, dataset = "logFC")  # Plot GSEA running enrichment gpsa_plot_gsea(gl_top, er_genes,                 main = paste0(top_hit, " vs Estrogen Response Early"))

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: Now let’s find perturbations activate interferon signaling.
code: # Get interferon alpha response genes ifn_genes <- get_hallmark_genes("HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE") message(sprintf("Interferon Alpha Response: %d genes", length(ifn_genes)))

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: find perturbations activate interferon signaling, use sign = +1:
code: # Define query: positive sign means we want perturbations where these genes go UP query_ifn_up <- list(   IFN_ACTIVATED = list(     genes = ifn_genes,     sign = +1,      # Looking for activation     weight = 1   ) )  # Run search out_ifn <- gpsa_search(db, query_ifn_up, return_components = TRUE)  # View top hits (perturbations that activate interferon response) message("=== Top 10 Interferon Activators ===") print(head(out_ifn$res[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName",                            "Score", "tau", "FDR_rank")], 10))

title: Get Started with GPSA
text: positive enrichment score confirms interferon response genes -regulated.
code: # Get the logFC profile of the top hit top_ifn <- out_ifn$res$signature_id[1] gl_ifn <- gpsa_get_signature(db, top_ifn, dataset = "logFC")  # Plot GSEA running enrichment gpsa_plot_gsea(gl_ifn, ifn_genes,                main = paste0(top_ifn, " vs Interferon Alpha Response"))

text: result table contains: Interpreting tau scores: - tau > 90: Strong positive connection (similar query) - tau < -90: Strong negative connection (opposite query) - tau ~ 0: significant connection

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
text: multiple related signatures (e.g., biological replicates, time points, related conditions), running individually inefficient. GPSA’s batch query feature: Runs multiple queries single matrix operation Computes query--query correlations Enables meta-analysis find consensus hits

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: library(GPSA)  # Set database path options(GPSA.h5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")  # Load database db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Choose multiple related signatures # Example: different perturbations of related genes sig_ids <- c("D21455", "D20287", "D23923")  # Replace with actual IDs  # Filter to those present in database sig_ids <- intersect(sig_ids, db$sigs) message(sprintf("Using %d signatures for batch query", length(sig_ids)))

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Create Up/Down query for each signature queries <- list() for (sid in sig_ids) {   gl <- gpsa_get_signature(db, sid, dataset = "logFC")   queries[[sid]] <- gpsa_make_updown_query(gl, n_each = 300) }  # Preview query structure names(queries)

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Run all queries at once bat <- gpsa_batch_search(db, queries, compute_tau = TRUE)  # View timing information message("=== Batch Query Timing ===") print(bat$timing)

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # The result contains: # - Score: matrix of scores (signatures x queries) # - tau: matrix of tau scores # - z_ref: matrix of z-scores for meta-analysis # - timing: execution time  dim(bat$Score)  # n_signatures x n_queries colnames(bat$Score)  # Query names

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Get results for a specific query query_name <- names(queries)[1] scores_q1 <- bat$Score[, query_name]  # Sort to get top hits for this query top_q1 <- sort(scores_q1, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10] message(sprintf("=== Top 10 for Query: %s ===", query_name)) print(top_q1)

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
text: Understanding similar queries helps interpret results.
code: # Compute correlation between query results cor_mat <- cor(bat$Score, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")  message("=== Query Similarity Matrix ===") print(round(cor_mat, 3))

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
text: queries represent related conditions, combine results find consensus hits.
code: # Stouffer's method combines z-scores across queries meta_res <- gpsa_meta_stouffer(bat$z_ref)  # View meta-analysis results message("=== Meta-analysis Top 20 ===") print(head(meta_res[, c("signature_id", "z_meta", "p_meta", "FDR_meta")], 20))

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
text: Interpretation: - High z_meta: Consistently high-scoring across queries - Low FDR_meta: Statistically significant consensus hit

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Define consensus: significant in meta-analysis consensus <- meta_res[meta_res$FDR_meta < 0.05, ] consensus <- consensus[order(consensus$z_meta, decreasing = TRUE), ]  message(sprintf("=== Consensus Hits (FDR < 0.05): %d ===", nrow(consensus))) print(head(consensus, 20))

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
code: # Check if a hit is consistent across queries candidate <- consensus$signature_id[1]  # Get individual scores individual_scores <- bat$Score[candidate, ] message(sprintf("=== Individual Scores for %s ===", candidate)) print(individual_scores)  # Get individual tau scores individual_tau <- bat$tau[candidate, ] message(sprintf("=== Individual Tau Scores ===")) print(individual_tau)

title: Tutorial: Batch Queries and Meta-analysis
text: queries different reliability, apply weights:
code: # Example: weight by sample size or confidence weights <- c(1.0, 0.8, 1.2)  # Adjust based on your criteria names(weights) <- names(queries)  # Manual weighted Stouffer z_weighted <- bat$z_ref %*% weights / sqrt(sum(weights^2))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: reference perturbation signature (-regulated -regulated genes), can search perturbations produce similar opposite transcriptomic effects. classic Connectivity Map (cMAP) approach. GPSA supports two methods selecting query genes: 1. Fixed selection: Take top N bottom N genes logFC 2. Adaptive selection: Use energy threshold determine optimal gene counts

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: library(GPSA)  # Set database path options(GPSA.h5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")  # Load database in memory mode db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: classic approach uses fixed number genes tail expression distribution.

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: # Choose a reference signature (e.g., an ESR1 perturbation) sig_ref <- "D21455"  # Replace with actual signature ID  # Get the logFC vector gl_ref <- gpsa_get_signature(db, sig_ref, dataset = "logFC")  # Preview the distribution summary(gl_ref)

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: # Create query with top 500 up-regulated and bottom 500 down-regulated genes query_ud <- gpsa_make_updown_query(gl_ref, n_each = 500)  message(sprintf("Up genes: %d", length(query_ud$Up$genes))) message(sprintf("Down genes: %d", length(query_ud$Down$genes)))  # Preview the query structure str(query_ud)

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: out_ud <- gpsa_search(db, query_ud, return_components = TRUE)  # Check if reference ranks highly (should be near top) self_rank <- gpsa_rank_in(out_ud$res, sig_ref) message(sprintf("Reference signature self-rank: %d", self_rank))  # Top 10 most similar perturbations message("=== Top 10 Most Similar ===") print(head(out_ud$res[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName",                           "Score", "tau", "FDR_rank")], 10))  # Bottom 10 most opposite perturbations message("=== Top 10 Most Opposite ===") print(tail(out_ud$res[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName",                           "Score", "tau", "FDR_rank")], 10))

what: Exclude Self to Find Similar Others
title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: # Find the most similar perturbation that isn't the reference itself top_other <- out_ud$res[out_ud$res$signature_id != sig_ref, ][1, ] message("=== Most Similar Other Perturbation ===") print(top_other[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName", "Score", "tau")])

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: Instead arbitrary cutoffs (500 genes), use energy-based thresholding automatically determine many genes capture given fraction signal.

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: # Select genes that capture 90% of the signal energy q_adaptive <- gpsa_make_updown_query_adaptive(   gl_ref,   eta = 0.90,      # Capture 90% of energy   min_n = 200,     # At least 200 genes per direction   max_n = 2000     # At most 2000 genes per direction )  # View selection information message("=== Adaptive Selection Info ===") print(q_adaptive$.info)  # The selected gene counts may differ from 500 message(sprintf("Adaptive Up genes: %d", length(q_adaptive$Up$genes))) message(sprintf("Adaptive Down genes: %d", length(q_adaptive$Down$genes)))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
code: # Note: Use only Up and Down, not the .info metadata out_adaptive <- gpsa_search(db, q_adaptive[c("Up", "Down")],                              return_components = TRUE)  # Compare self-rank with fixed approach self_rank_ad <- gpsa_rank_in(out_adaptive$res, sig_ref) message(sprintf("Adaptive self-rank: %d (vs fixed: %d)", self_rank_ad, self_rank))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: GPSA computes separate enrichment scores channels. can reveal whether hit matches directions just one.
code: # Attach per-channel scores to results res_channels <- gpsa_attach_channel_scores(   out_ud$res,    out_ud$NES_raw,    out_ud$NES_signed )  # View channel breakdown message("=== Top 5 with Channel Scores ===") print(head(res_channels[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "Score",                             "Up_raw", "Down_raw",                              "Up_signed", "Down_signed")], 5))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: hit Up_signed > 0 Down_signed > 0 shows concordant regulation directions (true phenocopy).

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: GPSA distinguishes two types hits: Phenocopy (Score_bi): channels must show expected direction (min signed scores) Discovery (Score_uni): least one channel shows strong signal (max signed scores)
code: out_modes <- gpsa_postprocess_modes(   out_ud,   attach_channel_cols = TRUE,   p_mode = "norm",   filter_positive = TRUE )  # Phenocopy hits: strict matches where both channels agree message("=== Phenocopy Mode Top 10 (Score_bi) ===") print(head(out_modes$res_similarity[, c("signature_id", "pbgene",                                           "Score_bi", "Score", "Score_uni",                                          "Balance", "Driver")], 10))  # Discovery hits: strong in at least one channel message("=== Discovery Mode Top 10 (Score_uni) ===") print(head(out_modes$res_discovery[, c("signature_id", "pbgene",                                         "Score_uni", "Score", "Score_bi",                                         "Balance", "Driver")], 10))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: Use cases: - High Score_bi + High Balance: True phenocopy, directions match - High Score_uni + Low Balance: One-sided hit, one direction matches - Driver column tells channel driving score

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: Validate hits examining running enrichment:
code: # Get logFC for a top hit candidate <- out_ud$res$signature_id[2]  # Second-ranked hit gl_cand <- gpsa_get_signature(db, candidate, dataset = "logFC")  # Plot enrichment for Up genes gpsa_plot_gsea(gl_cand, query_ud$Up$genes,                main = paste0(candidate, " vs Query Up genes"))  # Plot enrichment for Down genes gpsa_plot_gsea(gl_cand, query_ud$Down$genes,                main = paste0(candidate, " vs Query Down genes"))

title: Tutorial: Up/Down Bidirectional Query
text: Start fixed selection (n_each = 500) initial exploration Use adaptive selection want interpretable, energy-based cutoffs Always examine channel scores understand ’s driving hit Use dual-mode scoring need distinguish phenocopy discovery Validate top hits GSEA plots confirm biological relevance

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
text: /queries use extreme genes, vector search uses entire gene expression profile query. approach: Leverages information genes (just top/bottom) Uses rankZ transformation robust similarity Supports adaptive sparsification balance signal noise

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: library(GPSA)  # Set database path options(GPSA.h5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")  # Load database db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # Get a reference signature's full logFC vector sig_ref <- "D21455"  # Replace with actual signature ID gl_full <- gpsa_get_signature(db, sig_ref, dataset = "logFC")  # This contains logFC values for all genes length(gl_full) summary(gl_full)

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # The vector is named by gene symbol head(gl_full)  # Distribution of logFC values hist(gl_full, breaks = 50, main = "logFC Distribution",      xlab = "log2 Fold Change")  # How many genes have substantial changes? sum(abs(gl_full) > 1)  # |logFC| > 1 sum(abs(gl_full) > 0.5)  # |logFC| > 0.5

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: out_vec <- gpsa_search_vector(   db,    gl_full,   eta = 0.90,           # Capture 90% of signal energy   min_k = 300,          # Minimum 300 genes   max_k = 5000,         # Maximum 5000 genes   transform = "rankZ",  # Apply rankZ transformation   normalize = TRUE      # Normalize to unit length )  # Check self-rank (should be very high) self_rank <- gpsa_rank_in(out_vec$res, sig_ref) message(sprintf("Self-rank in vector search: %d", self_rank))

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # The compile info shows how the vector was processed message("=== Vector Search Compile Info ===") print(out_vec$compile)  # Key fields: # - k_used: number of genes retained after sparsification # - energy_captured: fraction of signal energy retained # - threshold: logFC threshold for sparsification

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: message("=== Vector Search Top 10 ===") print(head(out_vec$res[, c("signature_id", "pbgene", "CellLineName",                            "Score", "tau", "FDR_rank")], 10))

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
text: eta parameter controls much signal retain:
code: # High eta (0.95): Keep more genes, capture more signal out_95 <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, eta = 0.95, min_k = 300) message(sprintf("eta=0.95: %d genes used", out_95$compile$k_used))  # Lower eta (0.80): Keep fewer genes, focus on strongest signals out_80 <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, eta = 0.80, min_k = 300) message(sprintf("eta=0.80: %d genes used", out_80$compile$k_used))

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # Force at least 500 genes out_min500 <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, eta = 0.90, min_k = 500)  # Limit to at most 1000 genes out_max1000 <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, eta = 0.90, max_k = 1000)

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # rankZ (default): Robust to outliers, cMAP-style semantics out_rankz <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, transform = "rankZ")  # none: Use raw values (if already transformed) # out_raw <- gpsa_search_vector(db, gl_full, transform = "none")

what: Comparing Vector Search vs Up/Down Query
title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # Up/Down query with same reference query_ud <- gpsa_make_updown_query(gl_full, n_each = 500) out_ud <- gpsa_search(db, query_ud, return_components = FALSE)  # Compare self-ranks self_vec <- gpsa_rank_in(out_vec$res, sig_ref) self_ud <- gpsa_rank_in(out_ud$res, sig_ref)  message(sprintf("Self-rank comparison:")) message(sprintf("  Vector search: %d", self_vec)) message(sprintf("  Up/Down query: %d", self_ud))  # Compare top hits overlap top_vec <- head(out_vec$res$signature_id, 100) top_ud <- head(out_ud$res$signature_id, 100) overlap <- length(intersect(top_vec, top_ud))  message(sprintf("Top 100 overlap: %d signatures", overlap))

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
text: Compute squared values (energy) gene Sort genes energy (descending) Cumulative sum reaching eta fraction total energy Retain genes, zero rest
code: # Visualize which genes are retained compile_info <- gpsa_compile_signature_vector(   gl_full,    genes = db$genes,   eta = 0.90,   min_k = 300,   max_k = 5000 )  # The compile info shows threshold and genes used print(compile_info[c("k_used", "energy_captured", "threshold")])

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
code: # Which genes were kept? # Genes with |logFC| above threshold are retained threshold <- compile_info$threshold retained <- names(gl_full)[abs(gl_full) >= threshold]  message(sprintf("Retained %d genes with |logFC| >= %.3f",                  length(retained), threshold))  # Top retained genes by absolute logFC top_retained <- sort(abs(gl_full[retained]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:20] print(top_retained)

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
text: can also use gene list (database):
code: # Create a custom geneList from your experiment # Named vector: names = gene symbols, values = logFC my_genelist <- c(   "TP53" = 2.5,   "BRCA1" = 1.8,   "EGFR" = -1.2,   "MYC" = -2.0   # ... more genes )  # Search with custom list # Note: genes not in database will be ignored out_custom <- gpsa_search_vector(   db,    my_genelist,   eta = 0.90,   min_k = 10,  # Lower min for small gene lists   transform = "rankZ" )

title: Tutorial: Full Vector Search
text: large input vectors:
code: # If you have expression for all genes # The function automatically: # 1. Filters to genes present in database # 2. Applies sparsification # 3. Normalizes the query vector  # Check overlap with database genes overlap_genes <- intersect(names(gl_full), db$genes) message(sprintf("Genes in common with database: %d", length(overlap_genes)))

title: Tutorial: Multi-channel Event Definition (Viral Mimicry)
text: biological phenotypes captured single gene set direction. example, viral mimicry cellular state characterized : Interferon response genes (immune activation) Cell cycle genes (proliferation arrest) GPSA allows define multi-channel events combining multiple gene sets different expected directions.

title: Tutorial: Multi-channel Event Definition (Viral Mimicry)
code: library(GPSA) library(msigdbr)  # Set database path options(GPSA.h5 = "/path/to/gpsa_db.h5")  # Load database db <- gpsa_load_db(preload_Z = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)  # Get Hallmark gene sets hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H") get_hallmark_genes <- function(gs_name) {   unique(hallmark$gene_symbol[hallmark$gs_name == gs_name]) }

title: Tutorial: Multi-channel Event Definition (Viral Mimicry)

code: out_modes <- gpsa_postprocess_modes(   out_vm,   attach_channel_cols = TRUE,   p_mode = "norm",   filter_positive = FALSE  # Don't pre-filter, we'll examine both )  # Phenocopy mode: all channels must agree message("=== Phenocopy Mode Top 10 ===") print(head(out_modes$res_similarity[, c("signature_id", "pbgene",                                          "Score_bi", "Balance", "Driver")], 10))  # Discovery mode: at least one channel strong message("=== Discovery Mode Top 10 ===") print(head(out_modes$res_discovery[, c("signature_id", "pbgene",                                         "Score_uni", "Balance", "Driver")], 10))

title: GPSA - Gene-set Perturbation Signature Analysis
text: GPSA provides fast similarity search large-scale perturbation signature databases using cMAP/GSEA-style rankZ semantics.

title: GPSA - Gene-set Perturbation Signature Analysis
text: Large-scale perturbation experiments (e.g., CRISPR knockouts, drug treatments) generate thousands transcriptomic signatures. Given query gene set expression profile, researchers often need find perturbations produce similar opposite effects. Traditional connectivity map (cMAP) approaches require iterating thousands signatures, can slow. GPSA solves : Pre-computing rankZ-transformed signatures stored HDF5 format Enabling sub-second queries via optimized matrix operations Supporting flexible query types simple gene sets complex multi-channel events

title: GPSA - Gene-set Perturbation Signature Analysis
text: Drug repurposing: Find compounds reverse disease signature Mechanism discovery: Identify genes whose perturbation mimics phenotype Pathway analysis: Query pathway gene sets find relevant perturbations Cross-study comparison: Compare signature public perturbation databases

title: GPSA - Gene-set Perturbation Signature Analysis
text: GPSA uses rankZ semantics similar Connectivity Map methodology: Database signatures rank-transformed Z-scored (rankZ) Query gene sets compiled sparse indicator vectors direction signs Similarity scores computed via efficient matrix multiplication Statistical significance assessed using empirical null distributions (tau scores) approach captures relative ordering genes rather absolute expression values, making robust across platforms batches.
